lore_summary.en: The king who earned the worst name in the chronicle. Cruelty breeds only its mirror.
lore_summary.fa: یزدگرد گناهکار پدر بهرام گور، شاهی بود که روحانیون زرتشتی را به چالش کشید و به مسیحیان و یهودیان آزادی داد. اشراف از او می‌ترسیدند و دوستش نداشتند. مرگش در کنار چشمه‌ای نزدیک طوس رازآلود بود: اسبی ناشناس با یک لگد او را کشت و ناپدید شد — روحانیون آن را مجازات الهی خواندند.

scenes.body_en: The Zoroastrian priests gave Yazdegerd the title al-Athim — the Sinner — and the name stuck across centuries. He was Bahram Gur's father, the king Bahram had to both inherit and escape, and the Shahnameh's portrait of him is one of its most complicated: a ruler who was just to foreigners and unjust to his own, tolerant of Christians and Jews in an age when his clergy wanted persecution, and feared by his own nobles so thoroughly that they celebrated when he died.

What made him a sinner in Zoroastrian eyes was precisely what made him interesting to everyone else. He refused to let the fire-priests dominate the court the way they had under his predecessors. He gave Christians permission to build churches. He allowed Jewish communities to govern themselves under their own laws. He was, by the standards of his time and place, unusually pluralist — and the religious establishment hated him for it. When the Shahnameh calls him the Sinner, it is transmitting the clergy's verdict, not necessarily Ferdowsi's own.

His court was also dangerous to be near. He punished nobles harshly for real or imagined offenses. He trusted no one fully. The fear he inspired was not the productive fear of a king who rewards loyalty — it was the paralytic fear of a king who might decide at any moment that you had failed him. His nobles did not love him. They endured him.

His death, when it came, was strange enough to become theology. Near the city of Tus, at a spring, a horse appeared from nowhere — a horse of unearthly beauty that no one in the royal party recognized. Yazdegerd approached it. It kicked him once, in the chest, and vanished. He died where he fell. The clergy declared it divine punishment. The nobles who had lived in fear of him breathed again. His son Bahram, sent away to be raised in Arabia, came back to claim a throne still warm from a killing no one had expected and no one mourned.

battle.intro_en: The Shahnameh gave Yazdegerd a name — Sinner — and justified it at length. His cruelty produced its own punishment. To face this gate you must understand what the chronicle means when it names a king with his crime.
battle.intro_fa: شاهنامه به یزدگرد نامی داد — بَزِهکار — و آن را به‌تفصیل توجیه کرد. بی‌رحمیِ او کیفرِ خود را تولید کرد. برای مواجهه با این دروازه باید بفهمی دفتر هنگامی که شاهی را با جُرمش نام می‌برد چه مرادی دارد.

battle.intro_tg: Шоҳнома ба Яздигурд номе дод — Бадкор — ва онро ба тафсил асоснок кард. Бераҳмии ӯ ҷазои худашро тавлид кард. Барои рӯбарӯ шудан бо ин дарвоза бояд бифаҳмӣ солнома вақте ки шоҳеро бо ҷурмаш ном мебарад чӣ мурод дорад.
